problem.statement:
Detect water leaks in an instrumented pipe segment (inlet flow, outlet flow,
pressure; 1 sample/minute) as early as possible while keeping false alarms
rare. Constraint: detectors must be causal (no future data).

problem.statement:
Reduce false alarms in water-leak detection without losing leaks. Milestone 1 showed that
meter calibration bias and meter transport delay cause most false alarms. Test whether
causal per-day delay correction, daily baseline recalibration and alarm persistence fix
this, using pre-registered hypotheses judged on a held-out test set.

problem.statement:
STRESS TEST of the key Milestone 2 assumption: the daily calibration window is leak-free.
Here leaks may start at any minute, including inside the calibration window, so a
recalibrated detector can absorb the leak into its baseline. Measures how much the
Milestone 2 corrections lose when their assumption is violated.

hypotheses.statement: With leaks allowed in the calibration window, corrected+persistent threshold loses no more than 5 points of event recall
With leaks allowed in the calibration window, corrected+persistent CUSUM loses no more than 5 points of event recall
Corrections still reduce days with false alarms under this stress (threshold)

problem.statement:
CONFIRMATORY run on a FRESH synthetic dataset (seed 44, never used before).
The exploratory run (seed 42) showed that tuning converts the corrections' noise
reduction into sensitivity rather than fewer alarms. Hypotheses were reformulated
accordingly: compare detectors at a matched false-alarm budget (tuning objective) and
ask whether corrections buy recall, F1 and speed without paying in false alarms.
